supportPage.title: One person built ToolKnit. Help keep its free tools growing.
supportPage.lead: On March 18, 2026, one troublesome PDF became the starting point for ToolKnit. There was no team and no funding: regular work by day, real-world tools built at night. From the web app to the Windows desktop app, CLI, and MCP, one developer has continued to maintain the entire project.
supportPage.scanLead: To keep ToolKnit free and regularly updated for everyone, the author pays more than RMB 500 out of pocket each month for AI development and testing alone. Carrying this cost alone is becoming difficult. Every contribution directly funds continued maintenance, verification, and releases.
supportPage.supporterBenefit: Supporters may join the ToolKnit preview group, try early builds, and directly submit feature requests.
supportPage.voluntary: The preview group is for release discussion, testing, and collecting requests. Support does not purchase a feature, and no request is guaranteed or placed on a priority schedule.
supportPage.storyTitle: From one PDF to a publicly maintained toolbox
supportPage.storyBody1: It began as a way to solve a file problem close at hand. The web app later grew past 90 tools, while the Windows desktop app was built from the ground up with Rust and Tauri. Working a regular job by day and writing code at night, the developer handled features, compatibility testing, documentation, installers, and user feedback one item at a time.
supportPage.storyBody2: The desktop app was open-sourced on July 31, 2026. The next day it earned more than 150 GitHub Stars, one Douyin video reached 300,000 views and 6,400+ likes, and over 2,000 people used the web app. ToolKnit 2.0 rebuilt 49 desktop tools page by page and completed its CLI, MCP, and Agent workflows; V2.3 expands the desktop catalog to 65 tools.
supportPage.milestonesTitle: A few milestones along the way
supportPage.milestone1: Started with PDF tools and began publishing web updates.
supportPage.milestone2: Open-sourced the Rust + Tauri desktop app and brought the tools into local workflows.
supportPage.milestone3: ToolKnit V2.3 expanded to 65 desktop tools and hardened updates, dependencies, and compatibility.
supportPage.useBody: AI development and testing, compatibility hardware, dependency mirrors, documentation, installers, and continued open-source maintenance all carry real costs. Every contribution goes back into a more reliable next release.
supportPage.otherSupport: Donating is never required. Starring the repository, filing a reproducible issue, or sharing ToolKnit with someone who needs it is just as valuable.
supportPage.journalLead: Every release leaves a trace: the feature, the trade-off, the fix, and the real work behind keeping a one-person toolbox moving.

cDriveCleanupPage.title: C-Drive Cleanup
cDriveCleanupPage.subtitle: Clean system caches and temporary space in three risk tiers, with full impact details before every action.
cDriveCleanupPage.explainLowBody: These are caches and temporary files that the system rebuilds automatically. Cleaning them does not affect your personal files, sign-in state, or app settings.
cDriveCleanupPage.explainLowItems: User temp files, Windows temp files, browser cache, thumbnail cache, shader cache, crash reports, network cache
cDriveCleanupPage.explainMediumBody: Cleans update caches, delivery optimization, and logs. Some update components may need to be re-downloaded, but normal use is unaffected.
cDriveCleanupPage.explainMediumItems: Windows Update cache, Delivery Optimization cache, Windows logs, Developer caches
cDriveCleanupPage.explainHighBody: These system-level items free a noticeable amount of space but change the related system capabilities. Confirm before running.
cDriveCleanupPage.explainHighItems: Hibernation file, System restore points, Recycle Bin
cDriveCleanupPage.explainHighWarn: Turns off hibernation and fast startup (day-to-day shutdown/restart is unaffected and can be re-enabled); deletes existing system restore points (not recoverable, new ones will be created later); empties the Recycle Bin (not recoverable).
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedTitle: The following will not be cleaned
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedDesc: Cleanup targets only caches, temporary files, and system-space items. Your personal files are never scanned or deleted.
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedDownloads: Downloads, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Music, Videos
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedChats: WeChat / QQ chat history and files
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedBackups: WPS / Office backups and auto-recovery files
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedBrowser: Browser bookmarks, passwords, and sign-in state (only cache is cleared)
cDriveCleanupPage.protectedApps: Installed apps and their personal data
cDriveCleanupPage.adminDesc: C-drive cleanup touches system-level caches and requires ToolKnit to run as administrator.
cDriveCleanupPage.adminManual: You can also right-click ToolKnit in the bottom-right taskbar and quit, then right-click its desktop icon and choose "Run as administrator".
cDriveCleanupPage.adminUacCancelled: Administrator authorization was cancelled. ToolKnit will keep running normally.
cDriveCleanupPage.adminCheckFailed: ToolKnit could not confirm the current process permissions. Quit ToolKnit and try again.
cDriveCleanupPage.adminRequiredAgain: The current process does not have administrator rights. Authorize it before cleaning.
cDriveCleanupPage.confirmPermanent: Cleanup permanently deletes files and does not send them to the Recycle Bin.
cDriveCleanupPage.tips1: Start with the low-risk tier; move to medium or high risk only if you still need more space.
cDriveCleanupPage.tips2: Cleanup permanently deletes files and skips the Recycle Bin. Read the explanation on the right before confirming.
cDriveCleanupPage.tips3: Close programs that are using related files first, so files are not skipped because they are locked.
cDriveCleanupPage.howStep1Body: The page scans the recoverable space for each risk tier automatically; no manual folder selection is needed.
cDriveCleanupPage.howStep2Body: Choose low, medium, or high risk on the left; the right side shows what will be cleaned and the impact.
cDriveCleanupPage.howStep3Body: Review the confirmation dialog, wait for the 5-second countdown, then clean the selected tier in one click.
